Table 3 presents the housing characteristics of the unit before and after the upgrade. To assess the package’s effectiveness, we compared the performance of the unit with the full upgrade to its performance when each of the three individual measures was applied separately. Table 3. Housing Characteristics of the Example Dwelling Unit Before and After the Envelope Package Upgrades (Advanced Air Sealing + Attic Insulation + Duct Sealing and Insulation) Before Envelope Package After Envelope Package Housing Characteristics Upgrades Upgrades Infiltration 25 ACH50 5 ACH50 Insulation Ceiling R-38 R-60 10% Leakage to Outside, 5% Leakage to Outside, Duct Leakage and Insulation Uninsulated R-8 4.1.1 Individual Building Annual Results Figure 1 shows the annual energy consumption of the example dwelling unit under the full envelope package upgrade and under each of the three individual measures applied separately. Among these four scenarios, heating energy use shows the largest reduction, dropping from 105.5 MBtu in the baseline to 65.3 MBtu with the full upgrade, a 38% decrease. Cooling energy use also decreases slightly, while hot water energy use remains nearly unchanged. All other end uses are unaffected. The envelope upgrade reduced heat loss from the dwelling, which led to a slight increase in hot water energy consumption. In this example, the water heater is in an unheated basement. By preventing heat loss during winter and retaining cool air during summer, the upgrade improves overall thermal efficiency. However, because the unit is heating-dominated, the reduction in heat loss during winter is more significant than the benefit of retaining cool air in summer. As a result, less ambient heat is released into the unheated basement, causing the water heater to work harder and use slightly more energy to maintain the desired water temperature. The comprehensive envelope upgrade package reduces the dwelling unit’s annual total energy use from 165 MBtu to 122 MBtu, a 26% reduction. In contrast, advanced air sealing, duct sealing and insulation, and attic floor insulation individually reduced energy consumption by 18%, 8%, and 1%, respectively. This demonstrates that the full envelope package maximizes energy efficiency, highlighting the synergistic benefits of combining all three measures. 6 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications.
